subject: Real-traffic latency synthesis & decision memo (p95 / p99)
summary: Post-demo follow-up: confirm p95/p99 end-to-end targets under real traffic replay, reconcile hosted PoC numbers vs incumbent, and agree on a 4-hour shadow replay + 30-minute spike test. Decision criteria and action items outlined for sales/eng/CS alignment.
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@orionhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: poc@orionhealth.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: traffic profile and latency targets

Thanks, Sofia — great demo today. Attached is the traffic profile we mentioned (sampled hour, token distribution, user session patterns). Two asks from our side as we evaluate: 1) can Redwood reproduce our real traffic envelope (burstiness + long-tail prompts) and show p95/p99 E2E numbers for hosted API vs our incumbent provider; 2) propose an acceptance checklist (what failure modes you’ll instrument) so we can sign off on a migration decision.

Our initial target: p95 < 200ms end-to-end for single-turn summarize/chat flows; p99 ideally < 700ms. If you need different segmentation (short/long prompts, streaming vs sync) let me know.

Tim
Director, Platform Engineering — Orion Health

Attachments: orion_poc_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: traffic profile and latency targets

Thanks for the profile, Tim — useful shape. Quick recap and proposed path (we also attached an MAP draft):

- Short summary of PoC numbers (hosted API, default runtime, streaming enabled): p95 = 120ms, p99 = 420ms (end-to-end, measured from client TCP send to final chunk delivered) on the sampled hour replay we ran in the sandbox.
- Incumbent snapshot (your csv labels): p95 = 310ms, p99 = 1.15s. Those numbers match the logs you shared in the call.
- Key differences driving tail: prefix reuse (your traffic has high repetition for clinical templates), KV-cache misses on incumbent, and the incumbent’s conservative streaming chunk size + per-request orchestration hop.

What we propose next:
1) 4-hour shadow replay of the sampled traffic against hosted API (your creds in a shadow VPC) with request-level tracing and token-level timing enabled.
2) Add 30-minute synthetic spike window at 2x peak QPS to validate backpressure and autonomous fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized model.
3) Delivery of a short decision memo post-run with p95/p99 by prompt length bucket (<=128 tokens, 129-512, >512), streaming vs sync, and failure-mode checklist (timeouts, head-of-line queuing, 429s).

Ben/Jordan: can you confirm the instrumentation and the resource plan? I’ve proposed next-week windows in the MAP. Tim: once we align we’ll lock the dates.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (DOCX, 45KB), latency_breakdown_kpi.xlsx (XLSX, 82KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: traffic profile and latency targets

Adding the tech detail from the sandbox run and the proposed acceptance gates. High level metrics from our internal replay (matches Sofia’s summary):

- Hosted (default runtime):
  * p50 = 45ms, p95 = 120ms, p99 = 420ms (end-to-end, client->final token).
  * Sustained throughput: 600 RPS (single region), sustained token throughput ~1.2M tokens/min across cluster.
  * Concurrent streaming sessions handled: 140 with median per-client concurrency of 6 active streams.
- Incumbent (your logs):
  * p50 = 95ms, p95 = 310ms, p99 = 1150ms.

Instrumented probes we’ll enable during the run:
- Prefix/KV cache hit-rate per-token and time-to-first-byte when cache is warm vs cold.
- Per-request breakdown: network egress time (Redwood edge), model compute (per-token), aggregator/merge time, and client chunking latency.
- Headroom checks: queue depth, service concurrency, model warm-up cost under burst.

Acceptance gates (pass/fail criteria we recommend):
1) For short prompts (<=128 tokens): hosted p95 <= 180ms AND p99 <= 650ms.
2) For mid prompts (129-512): hosted p95 <= 300ms AND p99 <= 900ms.
3) No more than 0.5% of requests get 5xx or 429 during the 4-hour run; burst window can tolerate up to 2% transient flow-control 429s if automatic fallback to variant model succeeds and overall user-visible latency recovers within 30s.

If Ben’s numbers look reasonable to you, Jordan — next step is schedule and who owns the per-request traces from Orion’s side (we’ll need sampling keys).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Agree with Ben’s instrumentation and acceptance gates. I’ll own the decision memo template and the scoring rubric so the GTM/sales team can present a single recommendation to Orion leadership after the run. Quick notes on scoring and risk: 

- Scoring (0-100): latency (50 pts: weighted p95/p99 buckets), reliability (30 pts: error/429 rate + recovery time), operational risk (20 pts: config complexity, fallback validation). Target passing score >= 80.
- Commercial ask tied to result: if we meet the short prompt gate (<=128 tokens) and reliability gate, propose a 12-month dedicated commit at a blended rate (we’ll include a migration credit). If we fail by margin, recommend a 3-month staged migration starting with non-critical flows.

Operational owners: 
- Redwood: Ben (instrumentation lead), Sofia (customer comms + MAP), Infra (TBD) for the shadow VPC.
- Orion: Tim (trace keys + shadow access), Platform SRE (point person to accept test traffic).

Jordan will circulate the decision memo template by EOD. Proposed run window: May 25, 09:00-13:00 PT (4-hour run) with the 30-min spike at 11:30 PT. Please confirm availability.

—Jordan Blake
Head of Performance Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@orionhealth.com>

Appreciate the clarity — this plan works. We can provide trace keys and a service account for the shadow VPC. May 25 window is good for us; I’ll loop in our SRE point-of-contact and confirm the exact log sampling config (we want 100% request-level traces during the spike and 10% otherwise).

Two quick asks before the run: 1) can Redwood publish the exact SDK and runtime image tags you’ll use in the run so we can audit for parity with production? 2) can you include a short runbook section in the memo that explains the expected user-visible behavior during an automatic fallback (e.g., slightly lower fidelity quantized variant + user-facing note)?

Tim
Director, Platform Engineering — Orion Health
